title: US Day Traders Flock to Crypto's Riskiest Product as Perpetual Futures Go Mainstream
excerpt: Perpetual futures contracts — leveraged crypto bets with no expiration date — are now available to American retail investors after the CFTC opened the door, raising fears of amplified losses.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • CFTC approved crypto perpetual futures for US retail investors, enabling leveraged trading domestically.
  • Perpetual futures allow up to 50x leverage, risking total loss from just a 1% adverse move.
  • Billions are flowing into pre-IPO perpetual futures linked to SpaceX, ahead of major tech IPOs.
  • Major exchanges like Coinbase and Binance are rapidly launching perpetual futures products.
  • The CFTC has approved crypto perpetual futures for the first time in the US, allowing retail investors to access leveraged bets that were previously limited to offshore exchanges.
  • "Perps" have no expiration date and allow traders to borrow up to 50 times their stake, meaning a 2 percent adverse price move can wipe out an entire position.
  • Billions of dollars are flowing into pre-IPO perpetual futures tied to SpaceX, ahead of an expected wave of major tech IPOs including Anthropic and OpenAI.
  • Major exchanges including Coinbase, Binance and Kraken are racing to offer the products, while traditional exchanges like the NYSE's parent company have seen share price pressure from the competitive threat.

The Most Dangerous Product in Crypto

Perpetual futures contracts — the financial instrument that critics have called the most dangerous product in cryptocurrency — are no longer an offshore-only phenomenon. After the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission approved the products for domestic trading earlier this year, American retail investors have poured in, drawn by the promise of amplified returns and the lure of round-the-clock access to leveraged positions.

Unlike standard futures, which expire on a set date, perpetual futures — known as "perps" — roll over indefinitely. Traders can hold positions as long as they maintain collateral, and the contracts allow leverage of up to 50 times their initial stake on regulated US platforms. Some offshore venues offer leverage as high as 100 times.

The mathematics of that leverage are unforgiving. A 1 percent adverse move in the underlying asset can trigger liquidation — the automatic seizure of collateral — wiping out the entire position. In one recent 24-hour period, more than 254,000 leveraged positions were liquidated across global exchanges, according to crypto data platform Coinglass.

SpaceX Frenzy Fuels a New Product Category

The latest evolution has pushed perps beyond crypto assets and into equity-linked territory. Exchanges including Binance, Coinbase and Hyperliquid are now offering "pre-IPO perpetual futures" tied to SpaceX's valuation, giving traders a way to make leveraged bets on the company's future share price before it goes public.

The products have no direct link to actual SpaceX shares. They are priced with reference to the company's latest disclosed pre-IPO valuation, and billions of dollars have flowed into them. The popularity of these instruments has intensified the clash between crypto and Wall Street ahead of blockbuster IPOs expected from Anthropic and OpenAI.

When news broke that US regulators would approve crypto perps, shares of Intercontinental Exchange — the NYSE's parent company — dropped as investors weighed the long-term competitive threat to traditional exchanges.

"You don't have to think about where the market is, and losses could just compound and compound. That makes it that much more risky for retail investors."

— Ben Schiffrin, Director at Better Markets

How the Regulatory Door Opened

The CFTC's approval came through a policy framework allowing exchanges to offer perpetual futures tied to a broad range of digital commodities. Coinbase acquired crypto derivatives platform Deribit and received a no-action letter to provide US customers access to its product suite. Kraken spent $550 million to acquire Bitnomial and its perps offering. Kalshi received separate approval to offer Bitcoin perpetual futures directly.

The products operate through a "funding rate" mechanism that keeps contract prices aligned with the underlying spot market. Traders on the losing side of a price divergence pay a fee to those on the winning side, creating a self-correcting but costly system for those who hold positions through volatile periods.

What NRI and Diaspora Investors Should Know

For Indian-American investors and NRIs who may encounter perps through mainstream US platforms like Coinbase and Robinhood, the risk profile is fundamentally different from buying cryptocurrency directly. A spot Bitcoin purchase can lose value but cannot be liquidated overnight. A leveraged perps position can.

The CFTC has set leverage limits lower than offshore venues, but the products remain among the riskiest instruments available to retail investors. Consumer advocates argue that the combination of indefinite holding periods and extreme leverage creates a trap for unsophisticated traders who are attracted to the upside without fully understanding the downside mechanics.

With crypto exchanges aggressively marketing these products and traditional brokerages exploring entry, the perpetual futures market is likely to grow. Whether the regulatory framework can protect retail investors from the instrument's inherent dangers remains the open question.
